Place plane \(\mathcal P\) as the \(xy\)-plane and set

\[
A=(0,0,0),\qquad B=(6,0,0),\qquad C=(0,4,0).
\]

The centroid of \(\triangle ABC\) is

\[
G=\left(2,\frac43,0\right).
\]

The line \(BC\) has equation \(2x+3y=12\). Reflecting \(G\) across this line gives

\[
D=G-\frac{2(2\cdot 2+3\cdot \frac43-12)}{2^2+3^2}(2,3)
=\left(2,\frac43\right)+\frac{8}{13}(2,3)
=\left(\frac{42}{13},\frac{124}{39},0\right).
\]

The centers of the four spheres are therefore

\[
O_A=(0,0,1),\quad O_B=(6,0,2),\quad O_C=(0,4,3),\quad 
O_D=\left(\frac{42}{13},\frac{124}{39},r\right).
\]

A sphere tangent to both \(\mathcal P\) and a second plane \(\mathcal T\) has its center equidistant from \(\mathcal P\) and \(\mathcal T\). Thus all four centers lie in a common plane \(Q\), so \(O_A,O_B,O_C,O_D\) are coplanar.

Hence

\[
\det\begin{pmatrix}
6 & 0 & 1\\
0 & 4 & 2\\
\frac{42}{13} & \frac{124}{39} & r-1
\end{pmatrix}=0.
\]

Expanding:

\[
6\left(4(r-1)-2\cdot\frac{124}{39}\right)+1\left(0\cdot\frac{124}{39}-4\cdot\frac{42}{13}\right)=0.
\]

Simplifying,

\[
24r-\frac{976}{13}=0 \qquad\Rightarrow\qquad r=\frac{976}{312}=\frac{122}{39}.
\]

Thus \(m=122,\ n=39\), and

\[
m+n=122+39=\boxed{161}.
\]
